name: Department of Homeland Security
kicker: Cabinet department created after 9/11 · Runs the TSA, FEMA, and Coast Guard
briefing: After the September 11 attacks in 2001, Congress decided the country needed one department focused on protecting Americans at home from terrorism and disasters. The Homeland Security Act of 2002 combined 22 federal agencies, including the Coast Guard, the Secret Service, and the brand-new Transportation Security Administration, into the Department of Homeland Security, which opened in 2003 with former Pennsylvania governor Tom Ridge as its first secretary.
answerHtml: Department of Homeland Security (or DHS; accept Homeland Security; do not accept “Office of Homeland Security”)
accept: united states department of homeland security
reject: white house office of homeland security

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Early in 2001, the Hart-Rudman Commission recommended creating a new national agency to protect Americans from attacks on U.S. soil. Senator Joe Lieberman later pushed for a new cabinet department, and in June 2002, President George W. Bush proposed his own plan for one.
tossups.r: Congress created it later that year, after the September 11 attacks. For 10 points, name this department that oversees the TSA and FEMA.

tossups.p: A Vietnam War veteran who had been governor of Pennsylvania first led a White House office created in October 2001 to coordinate the fight against terrorism. In January 2003, that man, Tom Ridge, became the first secretary of this new executive department.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this cabinet department that includes the Secret Service and the Coast Guard.

tossups.p: The law creating this department was described as the biggest reorganization of the federal government since the National Security Act of 1947 created what became the Department of Defense. That 2002 law combined 22 federal agencies into this department.
tossups.r: Its first secretary was Tom Ridge. For 10 points, name this department formed after the September 11 attacks.

tossups.p: This department ran a five-color terrorism warning system that ranged from green for “low” to red for “severe.” In 2011, that system was replaced by the National Terrorism Advisory System, which issues bulletins and alerts instead of colors.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this cabinet department created after the September 11 attacks and first led by Tom Ridge.

tossups.p: After a 2006 plot to bomb airliners using liquid explosives, an agency in this department adopted its “3-1-1” rule, which limits the liquids passengers can carry onto planes. That agency had been created in November 2001 by the Aviation and Transportation Security Act.
tossups.r: That agency is the TSA. For 10 points, name this department that also includes FEMA and the Coast Guard.

tossups.p: Jimmy Carter created an agency in 1979 to lead the federal response to disasters, and it became part of this department in 2003. That agency, which also runs the National Flood Insurance Program, was widely criticized for its slow response to Hurricane Katrina in 2005.
tossups.r: That agency is FEMA. For 10 points, name this cabinet department, created in 2002, that was first led by Tom Ridge.

tossups.p: The only branch of the U.S. armed forces in this department traces its history to the Revenue Cutter Service, which Alexander Hamilton created in 1790 to stop smugglers. That branch moved into this department from the Department of Transportation in 2003.
tossups.r: That branch is the Coast Guard. For 10 points, name this department created after the September 11 attacks.

tossups.p: An agency founded in 1865 to fight counterfeit money moved from the Treasury Department into this department in 2003. That agency began protecting presidents full-time after the assassination of William McKinley, and it leads security at events such as presidential inaugurations.
tossups.r: That agency is the Secret Service. For 10 points, name this cabinet department created in 2002.

tossups.p: In 2003, the Immigration and Naturalization Service was abolished, and its jobs were split among three agencies in this department. One of those agencies, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, gives the civics test that most applicants must pass to become citizens.
tossups.r: Another, ICE, enforces immigration laws inside the country. For 10 points, name this department first led by Tom Ridge.

tossups.p: The U.S. Customs Service, created by one of the first laws passed by Congress in 1789, was combined with the Border Patrol in 2003 to form an agency of this department. That agency inspects travelers and goods arriving at airports, seaports, and border crossings.
tossups.r: That agency is Customs and Border Protection. For 10 points, name this department that also oversees the TSA.

tossups.p: In 2010, this department adopted a slogan first used by New York City’s transit system, “If You See Something, Say Something,” for a national campaign. In 2018, Congress created an agency within this department to defend government computer networks and vital systems such as power grids from cyberattacks.
tossups.r: That agency is CISA. For 10 points, name this department, created in 2002, that also runs the TSA.

tossups.p: Michael Chertoff, a former federal appeals court judge, was this department’s second leader. Janet Napolitano, a former governor of Arizona, became the first woman to lead it in 2009, and Jeh Johnson became its first African American leader in 2013.
tossups.r: Its first leader was Tom Ridge. For 10 points, name this department that includes FEMA and the TSA.

tossups.p: On November 25, 2002, President George W. Bush signed a law making this the 15th executive department of the federal government. It officially opened in January 2003, and most of its agencies moved into it that March.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this department formed in response to the September 11 attacks and first led by Tom Ridge.

tossups.p: Under the REAL ID Act of 2005, this department set security standards for state driver’s licenses and ID cards, and after years of delays, it began enforcing those standards at airport security checkpoints in May 2025.
tossups.r: Its Transportation Security Administration screens passengers at those checkpoints. For 10 points, name this cabinet department created after the September 11 attacks.

tossups.p: In February 2003, this department launched Ready.gov, a campaign urging families to build emergency supply kits and make plans for natural disasters and attacks. Every September, it promotes National Preparedness Month through FEMA, one of its agencies.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this department created by a 2002 law and first led by Tom Ridge.

Includes the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), which screens airline passengers
Includes FEMA, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, which leads the federal response to disasters
Also includes the Coast Guard and the Secret Service

trap.title: Department, office, or agency?
trap.body: This department is a big umbrella, and many of its parts have their own answer lines: the TSA, FEMA, the Coast Guard, and the Secret Service. A clue about airport screening or disaster relief might want that agency, not the whole department. It is also easy to mix it up with the FBI (part of the Justice Department), the CIA (an independent agency), or the White House office Tom Ridge led before the department existed.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun: “this department” or “this cabinet department” wants Homeland Security, while “this agency” or “this branch” wants the part being described. Clues about a 2002 law, 22 agencies combined, or the first secretary, Tom Ridge, point to the department.
trap.line: Real answer line: Department of Homeland Security (or DHS; accept Homeland Security)
